verses.text: Every person born of a woman lives only a short time, and life is full of trouble.
We grow up like a flower and then wither. We fade away like a shadow and do not last.
Do you really keep your eyes on someone like me? Will you bring me to court to be judged by you?
Who can bring something pure out of something unclean? No one!
You have decided how long a person will live. You have set the number of his months, and set limits he cannot go past.
So look away from him and let him rest, until he finishes his time like a hired worker.
There is hope for a tree. If it is cut down, it will sprout again, and new shoots will keep growing.
Its roots may grow old in the ground, and its stump may die in the soil,
but at the smell of water it will bud and put out new branches like a young plant.
But a person dies and is laid low. He breathes his last breath, and where is he?
As water disappears from a lake, and a river dries up and is gone,
so people lie down and do not rise again. Until the heavens are gone, they will not wake up or be woken from their sleep.
I wish you would hide me in the grave and keep me hidden until your anger has passed. I wish you would set a time to remember me!
If a person dies, will he live again? I would wait all the days of my hard service, until my release came.
You would call, and I would answer you. You would long for the creature your hands have made.
Then you would watch my steps, but you would not keep track of my sin.
My wrongs would be sealed up in a bag, and you would cover over my sin.
But as a mountain wears away and crumbles, and a rock is moved from its place,
as water wears down stones and floods wash away the soil, so you destroy a person's hope.
You overpower him once and for all, and he is gone. You change his face and send him away.
If his sons are honored, he does not know it. If they are brought low, he does not see it.
He feels only the pain of his own body, and he mourns only for himself."
